40b4a3598da1364e4d6ec9d1c8ff8ee01cbc347c.summary: IBM X-Force IRIS tracks ITG07, a threat actor that has intruded into geographically dispersed transportation-sector organizations over nine months. IRIS says ITG07 most closely aligns with activity other vendors call Chafer or APT39, which Symantec describes as an alleged Iran-based group. The report details a custom backdoor IRIS named TREKX, which NCCGroup reported in March 2019 as Chafer activity. ITG07 also uses legacy tools such as a custom Mimikatz, NBTScan, PsExec, webshells and remote access via Citrix, RDP and SSH-based tools. IRIS says ITG07 appears mainly engaged in surveillance…

hedges: IRIS says attribution to ITG07 rests on overlapping vendor data and TTPs that, with targets and infrastructure, make a compelling attribution case.
IRIS says ITG07 most closely aligns with activity other vendors report as Chafer or APT39, which is not presented as a confirmed match.
Symantec describes Chafer as an alleged Iran-based hacking group.
IRIS says TREKX is probably a custom remote access Trojan.
IRIS says no evidence in the environment allowed a definitive identification of the initial attack vector; the listed vectors are possibilities.
IRIS says ITG07 appears primarily engaged in surveillance and tracking of individuals, and that its attacks are likely carried out to gather information.
IRIS assesses it is very likely the transportation industry will continue to be a high-value target.
Two command-line options of an exfiltration RAT are listed with purpose unknown.
